title: Travon Walker Speaks on Extension, Career Trajectory w/ Media | Jacksonville Jaguars
text: Hi everyone. We have Trayvon Walker available. Please raise your hand if you have a question. We can start off with Jamal. What's up Trayvon? Congratulations, man. How's it feel to to kind of know that you're going to be in Jacksonville for for some time to come? My family was probably like 2-3 years ago. I was like if I can, I definitely love to be in Jacksonville for the rest of my career. Look at God. And Liam Cohen last week, he talked a little bit about your end of season meeting with him. Said you guys spent like 2 hours talking, talked about guys like Aaron Donald. What did you take from that conversation? Man, it's just like taking my game to another level. Obviously, he's he's seen Aaron Donald. He coached helped He was on the team with with Aaron Donald or whatever. So, it just kind of helped put things in perspective for me to be able to just click it to a different type of mindset was from how I was going throughout the year or whatever and I feel like that it really clicked dawned on me that it's just time to take wrap things up take take it to the next level. I do appreciate it Trayvon. Congratulations, man. Thank you. We'll go to D-Rock then to Shipley. Hey Trayvon, congrats. Was this a quicker process than you might have thought it would have been? Did you think this might be one of those you know, negotiations that kind of drag on for a while? Me personally, like I really didn't get too deep into the negotiation part. I just let my agent handle that and they did what they did what they did and I mean it was going to happen on God's timing anyways. I'm firm believer in God and everything. It just took it took its own it did its own race. Does it take a weight off your mind at all that it's done now and that you don't have to we're not asking you about it in June, July, August and stuff? I mean I definitely say it takes some weight off of my mind. Not not saying that I was really too concerned about it cuz I mean eventually I know it was going to happen regardless of however much or whatever, but just like having it out of the way the money part all of the talks about the money like it's just time to go play ball now. I don't have to think about none of that. Like I said, it's just time to go play ball now. And one more real quick back to what Jamal was saying about Liam talking about Aaron Donald. He said he wants to have to take you out of practice because you're destroying their practice and ability to practice. I mean how What does that mean to you? I mean that that's got to be pretty high praise when he mentions you and Aaron Donald and says yeah, Aaron Donald made it so we couldn't practice and now I want Trayvon to do the same thing. It's just predominance, man. It's it's just also it's it's helping everybody else on the team get better while it's helping me get better as well. Like I said, it's just predominance and everybody that plays in this league wants to be great, wants to be hopefully that's everybody's mindset to be great in the end and I think that's that's really what he was getting to when he was speaking on that. Thanks bud. Appreciate it. Sir, thank you. Shipley then to O'Halloran. Shipley, I think you're still muted. Oh, sorry. Trayvon, congratulations and thanks for doing this. You said that you know, you've known for a few years that Jacksonville is where you wanted to be. What does it say to you that you know, even with new people coming in last year, they pretty quickly showed that same belief in you that they wanted you here? Can you say that one more time for me? Sorry. Yeah, you said a few that you knew for a few years that this is where you wanted to be. What does it say that even with a new coach, new GM coming in you know, just a year ago that did you pretty quickly they it was a mutual feeling that they wanted you here too? It really means a lot cuz like you say getting a new staff in like you it's always that uncertainty and coming into the when they first got here, I I feel like they did a great job of just communicating with me think of things and that kind of already put in perspective to how that relationship was going to go. Sometimes you never really know how it's going to go, but ever since they've been there, I feel like we on my end and their end we've been transparent with each other and we just have cordial conversations to where we can all just be comfortable and that was one of Liam's main things that like say what's on it speak your mind and we'll go from there. And I feel like >> Appreciate it Trayvon. Yes, sir. Hey Trayvon, a couple for you. Late in the season, they moved you inside on some passing downs next to Josh. If you guys start doing that for the full season, what kind of impact do you think you could have as an interior rusher? I think I can have an impact wherever they put me. I don't care if they put me in in the secondary. It's all about versatility in this league or whatever, but it's all about just being versatile do whatever the team do whatever I need to do to help the team. So, a blitzing safety is on the table? Say that again. A blitzing safety is on the table? >> Hey, if that's what we need then I'll do whatever. Last [clears throat] one for me is you had a lot of pressures last year. Your pressure rate was was pretty decent. What are you working on this off season to to take that next step to to get back to that double double digit sack totals? Number one my main thing was just working on getting healthy and then it's just fine tuning those little small details within my hands, eye coordination, things of that nature. Just trying to keep my twitch as far as my strength, wrist mobility, working on some a lot of things, but it's basically just kind of ironing out some small details. You know, the further you get in your career like it kind of get it gets harder to I wouldn't say it gets harder to continuously elevate. It's just like you got to find those little small little details within your game and continuously work those things. Thank you now. Last one, Travis Holmes. Congratulations on the extension Trayvon. I just wanted to know like how has your leadership style evolved since you first initially entered the league as a number one pick and now you have the opportunity with the extension and everything else and just being that leader on the field to also mentor the younger players. Man, I think for me it's just kind of a I wouldn't even say a more vocal me. It's just like obviously leading by example. I know what what's expected in the league. I know what's expected from a leadership standpoint. I know what's expected from this this staff that we have and I just try to go out there and be the best version of me every day and I feel like I've been a leader at my whole life. So, a lot of things just really translate to talking to the players players coming to me asking questions. It's just about me opening up telling them things that I went through. Just maybe say if I was a rookie or whatever, but that's really all it is. No, appreciate it. And also with the two the back-to-back two sack seasons and then having the multiple injuries dealt dealt with in this past you know, 2025 season like how did that impact you or did that impact you at all in you know, as far as the mental as far as your off season preparation and all of that? I mean it definitely affected me with the injuries, but just coming out going having two back-to-back double digit sack seasons then coming off a season like last year. It's just always I mean it's football. It's a 100% injury rate. You know those injuries going to be there, but you just got to continuously fight through those things and that's what I tried my best to do and like long as I'm not putting the team in a bad position in my eyes to jeopardize winning games or whatever. I'm going to always try my best to be out there on the field regardless of banged up hurt or not cuz everybody around the league at a certain point in the season is going to be banged up at some point. So, I just try to keep going. I appreciate you. Congratulations. Sir, thank you. That's everyone. Thanks, Tray. Thank you all.

title: Travon Walker Reacts to Contract Extension | Jacksonville Jaguars
text: Brian Ston in the draft room with newly ressigned Trayvon Walker. Congratulations. What a blessing on Easter weekend. >> 100% beyond blessed. Uh God God without God, it wouldn't have been none of this. And uh like to thank the everybody in the front office from the coaches to to everybody, man. It's it's mindblowing. I wouldn't want to be nowhere else. >> I was going to say, what does it mean to you to resign with a franchise that you've only ever known in your professional career to know that you'll be here? >> It really means a lot. Uh, it just goes to say for me, I always wanted to be here. Like you said too, I was drafted here as well. So, this is all I know. I feel like a lot of my blood, sweat, and tears that I put into this is to help kind of get this organization with along with other players as well to get this organization where we want to go in the future, which is the Super Bowl, and that's something that I'm I really want to help bring to this city. I feel like that'll be major. >> What does it say to you that last two years they've gotten Trev uh Trevor Dunn, uh Josh Dunn, now you're part of that fold. They're building a new stadium. They've got a new office building. This whole thing has been under construction. And to be a part of that, >> uh, it really means a lot to be a part of that. Like you said, like you said, really with the stadium, it makes a lot of sense, too, cuz we've, this team has just been getting better and better as ever since I've been here. And you see the foundation being poured into that stadium. It's it's similar to what the players are bringing into this building, the coaching staff is bringing into this building, the guys in the front office. So you can tell everything the trajectory of what we want here in Jacksonville is everything's going in the right trajectory. >> You got it out last season. First the wrist in San Francisco, then the knee injury that you suffered against the Chargers. How do you feel now? What is your prognosis for the offseason program? >> Feel pretty good. Uh this offseason I just been working on my strength with my wrist and getting my my range of motion back. Uh like I said, I feel healthy now. Uh I'm ready to go, man. Got this got this done and now I'm ready to get back out there on the field with the guys and get to work. And this defense took a massive step forward last year under coach Campanily. What are your expectations for where you're headed this year? >> Uh just to continually grow from picking up where we left off last year. Uh no no drop off. We just want to continually get better 1% every day. You know, that's the motto and uh that's what we're going to do. Uh it's no we can't it's no going backwards. >> First season under Liam Cohen from 4 and 13 the year before to 13 and four. What does success look like for this team going forward? I think for us it's just continuously to like I said just continuously to build off of what we've been doing. Uh it's we don't have to go out doing too much search and things of that nature in my opinion. I just feel like we keep building on the things that we've started to implement into this organization and I feel like we'll be perfectly fine. Just keep believing within each other and buying in long as we buy in everybody we all have the same goal in the end and that's to win games and we know the end goal which is Super Bowl and everything else take care take care of itself. What did Tony Belli or James Gladstone or Liam Cohen say to you when they got this deal done? They they talked to the media, Trayvon, about you being a big part of the Jaguars DNA. What conversations did you have with them leading up to this? >> We had so we uh my only time I really really had a conversation with them was my ex and meeting uh conversation and all of them was just like they really want me to get to that point to where it's just pure dominance. they know I have it in me and uh that's something I love I love hearing that coming from them them and uh it holds me to a high standard which I really like that they going to stay on me stay coaching me hard and it's not just one of those things to where obviously it's the NFL you don't get a lot of coaching or a lot of talks from a lot of your staff members but that's how you know that they really care and u man it's it's been a journey uh it was a long journey but we're here we came to agreement and I'm happy for that >> let's end with this uh Your family surrounded you here as you signed this contract today. Your family is big and an important part of your life. What did it mean to you today to have all of them present? >> Uh it really means a lot to me. Uh family is everything to me. Um it's God first and me and my family. Without my family, I wouldn't even be in this position. Uh to be able to be this athlete that I am from genetics to how they raised me. It really means a lot. And just to have them surrounding me, man, like I have my younger niece here. I really wanted her here just so she can, you know, be a part and see things like this cuz she plays sports as well. and not just my niece, but my mom. I know she's proud of my dad and my sisters as well. They put a lot of hard work into the development of me as well outside of the field. Congratulations, sir. Thank you.

title: ‘Completely in Command’: Fernando Mendoza’s Pro Day Recap
text: You're listening to the Raiders NFL Draft Podcast. Here are your host, Bucky Brooks and Rhett Lewis. Raider Nation, welcome back. The Raiders NFL Draft Podcast is up and running once again and coming to you following what I would call the capstone performance in the draft profile of presumptive number one pick Fernando Mendoza. Coming off the Indiana Pro Day, uh I was there in person. I'm Red Lewis, of course, Bucky Brooks, former Raider, former NFL scout with us as always. And um Bucky, we were both on the broadcast for NFL Network of the Proday and uh it was it was quite a scene out there. I mean, I can tell you as a former Indiana Hooer, it was the biggest proday in the history of Prodays at IU. That I can tell you for sure. What was your kind of view of what it all kind of looked like from your perspective? >> So, I think there are a few things that are interesting when it comes to proday. People talk about pro days aren't a big deal, but I think you can uh follow the breadcrumbs in terms of what people are thinking based on how they treat the proday. So, from the Raiders side, it was a large contingent there. You saw John Spek, you saw Kubiaak, uh there were 10 officials there to see and what you want is you're trying to get a full assessment of the people that you're looking at. And we'll talk about Fernande Mendoza primarily. Everyone wants to have an opinion. You want to weigh. You want to make sure you get different perspectives on how everybody felt like he performed, how he handled the interactions with his teammates and those things. For Fernando, this is like the biggest job interview that they have. Despite all the things that he's done, all the things that he's put on tape, the interview that he had at the combine, there's a different pressure that comes to being able to perform on a pro day. And even though we can talk about it being the equivalent to going to the driving range and hitting a small bucket of balls, you still want to show the people that are the decision makers that you have all the goods to be that. And I think, look, he knocked it out the park. his interactions with his teammates, the way that he commanded and barked out orders to his wide receivers and the other eligible pass catchers that were there showed leadership, but then the connectivity that they displayed at the end of it. The way his people really feel connected to Fernando to me, that's really what you're trying to see because we can assess all the things on tape, but what you can't get a true assessment of is how are they going to fit the culture and the environment that has already been established. >> Yeah. Yeah, look, you're not going to draft Fernando Mendoza number one overall based on the fact that he threw a 65 yard absolute dime by the way deep shot on the money to EJ Williams down the field. It's great to see, but that's not why he's going number one overall. All of those types of things you see when you watch his 16g game undefeated, you know, run as the quarterback of the national champion Indiana Hoosiers. That's all out there for you. Um, you know, the way he reacts to defenses, the way he reacts to prep, that's all there for you. That's not what you're gaining here at Proday, but what you were talking about, part of what I got a chance to talk to John Spitech about there in Bloomington on Wednesday was the way he interacts, the way he runs it, the way he commands it. Um, now look, I think there's certain things about accuracy that you can see there. Obviously >> throwing, you know, routes on air essentially. you want to be dang near perfect. And he was uh maybe there's one ball that he kind of overthrew just a touch, one that kind of lost a little bit of fluttered a little bit in the air, but again, those are those are so minor. All that stuff is so minor. Like it was from a throwing perspective, it was excellent. But what really stood out and you kind of touched on it was one his command of the moment. He was saying, uh, you know, Elijah, you're running the inside shake or Omar Cooper, you're running the whip. uh you know, Riley Noakowski, the tight end, you've got the uh you you know, you've got the the the deep curl, like all those sort of things, like he was in charge. He wasn't even like looking on the on the script, too. It was all up here in recall. The way he supported his teammates the whole day. He wasn't doing any of the testing, but he was there for them while they were uh encouraging them, that sort of thing. And then this whole I got a chance to kind of go behind the scenes with him a little bit the week before the proday and this was a coordinated effort not only to showcase what he felt like he wanted to accomplish, but to let his teammates showcase their skills in front of all 32 teams. And I I thought one of the things he mentioned to me in our interview afterwards was he was like, "Look, I I hope this is, you know, this is kind of the last time in Bloomington, but I hope I get to play against and play with some of these guys in the future because that is certainly a possibility um as we go forward with some of the other players like Omar Cooper, Elijah Serat, Riley Noacowsky, the running backs Kalon Black and Roman Hembi. Um EJ Williams, another receiver who kind of showed up in a big way uh in that workout. But for Fernando, this was excellent. Um, he was he was every Now, the the other thing that that did sta stand out, and I want to hit you on this size, Bucky. >> This is a 6'5 quarterback that weighed in at 236 pounds and looked every bit of it. >> Thick, firm, strong lower half. You could tell in his forearms that there's some extra muscle that has been built here. He was telling me it was he's up 7 lbs and down 7% body fat uh since the national championship game. You know who's also 6'5 and 237 pounds? Josh Allen. I'm not saying that Fernando is is you know moves the way Josh Allen does but like that frame plays man he is a prototypical quarterback. What was your take on that part of it? You know, I think that's the thing you checked off the boxes when it talks about the prototype. And a lot of times when we are doing what we call body typing, uh, assessing what a player looks like when they walk beside us or behind us, in front of us, we are not only looking at like the frame and the features and those that, but are they in shape? Has he taken the process seriously? has he really committed to be in shape or has he been on the banquet circuit just kind of hanging out and meling it in because he assumes and everyone assumes that he's gonna be the number one and what I would say is I'm probably more impressed with the way that he walked in the way that he looked the work that you could tell that he's been doing that's struck with me the thing that also stood out to me is in the interview that he talked to with you he talked about I did not want this to be a flashy proday where we're doing pro proday stuff I wanted to show that we're getting ready to play and that the >> pro day had a I would say a professionalism to it. It had uh a bit of the process that he always speaks to like hey here's where I'm at in my journey. Here's where I'm at and this is where I'm trying to go. So let me do some things under center. Let me show you that I've worked on this stuff and I've continued to work on it in preparation for mini camp and training camp and the regular season and the things that lie ahead. So to me, the more that I'm exposed to Fernando, the more that I like him in terms of his approach, his process, the professionalism, and I will say this, the overall presidential feel that he has as the leader in the face of a franchise down the road. >> Completely in command. By the way, the pace of that workout was I I mean, it was moving. The tempo was hot in there. And it was warm in there, too. like and and it was allowed to kind of go that fast because they had nine different guys that he was throwing to. So, you didn't have to wait for the receivers to kind of catch their breath. There was a constantly another one going and they had that script man coordinated again. It was they they had prepared it really well. Um and then just on the size thing when I was with him in Irvine watching him work out uh before he left for Bloomington, you know, bunch of guy people are always coming up to him, right? He's always very gracious with that stuff. I I thought it was kind of cool. Some of the groundskeepers at one of the schools where he was throwing at came up to him, started talking Spanish to him, and he started talking Spanish right back, held the whole conversation, took photos. But that those guys, the high schoolers that came out to watch him. All of them were remarking at how big he was. He's like, "Whoa." They're all like, "Whoa, you look you're way bigger in person." Well, he he's he's gotten bigger and he he got bigger from the moment he got to Indiana. like he was he he played this season bigger than he did at Cal and then he's gotten he's added more good weight to his frame. And let's not forget like he moves around pretty well now. He's got some mobility that can win you can get you first downs and as we saw in the national championship can help you win games. Um but it can get him out of a trouble trouble a little bit. And then I think as we learn more about, you know, the connection with the Raiders and with Clint Kubak, he throws really well on the run, Bucky. And that was something he wanted to showcase in this proday script as well. And that's something I think we're going to see here eventually within this Raiders offense is and that's kind of been a staple of that that this style of offense is the ability to get out there on some of those boots and uh some of those nakeds and make those throws. >> Yeah, I think it's really important. And the reason why it's important is because so much of the system that Kubak has employed and the offshoots of this system that was employed by his dad Gary Kubak and Mike Shanahan features a lot of play action, a lot of movement passes, a lot of misdirection with shots taken back side. You talked about, we've talked about the 65 yard toss that he delivered on a dime. Some of those things were staples of Gary Kubak's offense back with the Houston Texans and they've been sprinkled in Clint Kubak system when he's been able to run an offense. I think we'll see that. But watching Fernando go through everything. Shotgun, under center, the tosses that he was making, those are things that you can visualize him doing with the Las Vegas Raiders. I think if you're the Raiders brass, you have to be excited about his process. You got to be excited about his progress from the end of the season to now. And then you have to be excited about what could take place going forward now that you're beginning to put your ducks in the road to set them up for long-term success. Couple of a couple other things about the value of a proday, right? And the ability to have a a really, you know, kind of unregulated uh touch point with him, right? There's not a lot of constraints on what you the time that you can spend around him in this setting where there are in some of the other ones with the Zooms that you do. Obviously, in the combine interview, it's so truncated, 15, 18 minutes, that sort of thing. They got a chance to obviously be around him the entire day, watch him throw. uh he had a meeting with Clint Kubak right after the workout that he was going with. Then they all had dinner together there in Bloomington as a contingent. Um and and so like the value of that time to kind of just be around and really kind of get to know him better than maybe you have at any time elsewhere in the process. H you know from your experience as a scout like how how do you kind of value that time that you can get out of proday with a player in a situation like this? Oh, you value it um a ton because you don't know the player. We've only been exposed to the player briefly. Small interactions. Talk about the official form interview that you have at the combine. Maybe your pro your your scout has kind of met Fernando in passing when he's visited the school and those things, but you still haven't had an opportunity to fully build out a relationship. Now, the league is different where you have some Zoom calls, but it's still nothing like face-toface interactions. And so for the Raiders to be able to get that, it makes them feel more comfortable about who the player is. And before we talk about like what they do on the field, it's really the comfort in the player, who you're coaching, who you going to bring in, who you're going to entrust to be the designated leader of the team. You have to be really comfortable with the personality and you have to develop a level of trust in that player because no matter what people say, not only does he carry the weight of being the number one overall pick if he's selected by the Raiders, but he's QB1, the new face of the franchise. That is significant and you have to make sure that you can trust him with all those responsibilities. >> Yeah. I I just uh continue to be really impressed with the way that he carries himself. you know, one of the questions I was asking him um in our conversation after uh the workout, you know, was was about the Raiders and about all of the external speculation about going number one. Um and he has obviously done his best to to kind of block that out. But I I also kind of pressed him on, look, you got a lot of people you're trying to make an impression on, many of which are here. general manager John Spyc, head coach Clint Kubak, offensive coordinator Andrew Janoko, who by the way played with Indiana quarterbacks coach Tino Sinceri, and offensive coordinator and wide receiver coach Mike Shanahan when they were all together at Pit, which is which is kind of a cool connection. So they'll they'll really get the full spectrum of who uh Fernando is with some of those connections. But um you know I was asking him obviously about those guys and then you know most notably about minority owner Tom Brady who it's no secret Fernando he's kind of been Fernando's idol uh in terms of football guys that he looks up to and watches. And so I was like what is what is something about you that you want to make sure Tom Brady in addition to this entire Raiders evaluation staff knows about you as a quarterback? And I I thought the the answer he gave was pretty powerful in that he's like, "Look, no matter what's happening in this process, no matter how many people put my name next to the Raiders at number one overall in a mock draft or talk about me going number one overall or as the number one quarterback in this class, I am always going to be the same person, the same Fernando Mendoza, which is something that I can vouch in the time that I have spent around him and around his teammates. He is literally everything to everyone, always the same dude. Um, and he is truly authentic and he is always focused on the task at hand. And I think those are things that Tom can really relate to. Tom was incredible uh at blocking out the noise, preparing maniacally, right? And focusing in on what the task at hand was each and every day, each and every rep, each and every play, each and every game, each and every season. And that's really at the core of who Fernando is. So, I think that that message will probably get relayed back to Tom because he was not uh in Bloomington. As far as I could tell, I don't know if he was there in sunglasses and a mustache or something, but as far as I could tell, Tom was not one of the 10 Raiders personnel that were there, but I just I think that's something that really will impress Tom and will be a part of that decision-making process. >> Yeah. No, I think it has to be a big part of it. And you talk about being able to uh be the same to maintain it. And I think it continues to speak to what Fernando always uh talks about and that's being processoriented because when you're processoriented, you worry about the task at hand. You don't worry too far ahead. You don't worry about what just happened. You're focused on being the best that you can be today and improving upon the task that you have in front of you. So, you love that. You love to hear that. And I do believe that Tom will uh find comfort in knowing that Fernando's mentality and mindset is on the here and now. And I think the other thing at a time where so many young people and so many young players coming into the league can worry about other stuff like brands and and the the the auxiliary stuff around the game. >> Fernando is very committed and focused on the game because if you focus on the game, the other stuff will come. And I think he is wellwired to be a QB1 in this league for a franchise as distinguished as the uh Las Vegas Raiders. >> Yeah. Yeah. Uh I want to get to a couple more things on Fernando and then hit the Kirk Cousins news which is fresh here as we're recording here today and then uh bounce out of here uh for this episode. Um but with Fernando, a couple things that I've learned just talking to his teammates. Um, number one, like I asked a bunch of them, you know, when did they know that he was going to be the dude? Like when did they know he was like a guy, right? Like a football dude that could lead them to the promised land. Uh, Aiden Fischer told me, Aiden Fischer's a linebacker, really good player. He's going to get drafted, um, in my opinion. And he was like, I was giving Fernando so much crap. I was talking so much, you know what, to Fernando through the first couple of practices of spring ball and he just kind of took it, right? We kind of ignore it, walk away, move on. Um, and then by practice five, Fish said Fernando was talking some stuff back and carving the defense up. And at that moment, Fish was like, "Okay, like we got a dude." Which which kind of brings, you know, one of the final pieces of the Fernando evaluation to me. He is a million-dollar smile with a make you pay mentality. He will rip your heart out and do it with a smile on his face. Coach Signetti called him in addition of one of the most uh well-prepared players he's ever coached an absolute lion of a competitor. That toughness really resonates with his teammates. Um and that's the other piece that I wanted to convey. Uh Pat Gooan, his center, another player is going to get drafted this year said that it was the Iowa game. It was the scramble on third and 15 in which he picked up almost the entire first down, got 14 of the 15 and then got absolutely plastered on the sideline by an Iowa defender, bounced right back up and ended up obviously leading a game-winning touchdown drive in that game. um that toughness he showed in that game on a play like that, on a run like that that put his body on the line to try and get a first down, that moment and then the culmination of the result of that game really endeared him to his teammates. He is such a magnetism to them. One, because he connects with them, but two, because of moments like that. And then there was the Heisman Trophy thing. Last thing I'll say on it, um, that night those guys have said even maybe even more so than celebrating the national title was like the best night of their lives was to celebrate Fernando in New York winning the Heisman. In fact, it is the name of their group text thread now is thank you Fernando. Like that's how much his teammates, you know, love him and appreciate the player he is. So thought that was really cool. Uh lastly, do want to hit on Kirk Cousins, the veteran quarterback now coming in uh to join the Las Vegas Raiders on a what's basically a one-year deal. The contract details that have been reported are a little bit convoluted. You could call it a 5year $170 million deal, but there's void years. There's a two-year $80 million option, but it's essentially a one-year $20 million deal that's fully guaranteed with the Atlanta Falcons playing a vast majority of that deal.
